glosses: The act of guarding and observing someone or something.

examples.text: shepherds keeping watch by night

examples.text: The second watch of the night began at midnight.

examples.text: The watch stopped the travelers at the city gates.

glosses: The post or office of a watchman; also, the place where a watchman is posted, or where a guard is kept.

examples.text:

 Brave me upon the watch.

glosses: A group of sailors and officers aboard a ship or shore station with a common period of duty: starboard watch, port watch.
A period of time on duty, usually four hours in length; the officers and crew who tend the working of a vessel during the same watch. (FM 55–501).
The act of seeing, or viewing, for a period of time.

examples.text: Watching the clock will not make time go faster.

glosses: To observe over a period of time; to notice or pay attention.

examples.text: Watch this!

glosses: To mind, attend, or guard.

examples.text: Please watch my suitcase for a minute.

glosses: To be wary or cautious of.

examples.text: You should watch that guy. He has a reputation for lying.

glosses: To attend to dangers to or regarding.

examples.text: watch your head; watch your step

examples.text: The senator observed that the bill would be detrimental to his constituents.
